exposure: Number of vaginal delivery simulation training sessions (two, three, four, or five 45-minute sessions)
outcome: Attainment of minimal competence in vaginal delivery
Attainment of mastery in vaginal delivery
cohort: 115 third-year medical students at a US medical school participated in the study.
finding: The amount of simulation training provided to medical students had an increasing effect on their performance, with higher numbers of sessions leading to improved checklist scores and a greater proportion achieving mastery in vaginal delivery skills.
mod_finding: Simulation training significantly improved medical students' competence and mastery in performing vaginal delivery.
